newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 13.0/13.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 13.0/13.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 13.0/13.5 percent on Tuesday late morning on the back of sufficient liquidity, dealers said.
They said there was a brief uptrend at the opening, with rates rising to a high of 15.5 percent before easing.
The central bank supplied 453 billion rupiah on Tuesday.
One local bank dealer said demand for one-week money was higher than usual because it will mature on Tuesday, July 15, when weekly tax payments will due and be larger than usual.
She said preparations to meet payments due around that period caused longer-term rates to firm. One-week money was at 13.5 percent and one-month was at 13.375 percent.

The central bank offered seven-day bilateral papers (SBIs) at seven percent, two-week at 8.25 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent, three at 10.75 percent, six at 11.25 percent and 12-month at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rates on Monday was 15.79 percent, compared with 15.93 percent on Friday.
